rule: Discuss already means talk about. It takes no about.
wrongEx: We will discuss about the budget tomorrow.
rightEx: We will discuss the budget tomorrow.

right: I will get back to you
rule: Revert means return to an earlier state. Back repeats it. To answer someone, reply or get back to them.
wrongEx: Kindly revert back by Friday.
rightEx: Kindly reply by Friday.

rule: You borrow FROM someone. Someone lends TO you.
wrongEx: Please borrow me your pen.
rightEx: Please lend me your pen.

rule: The verb is cope with. There is no up.
wrongEx: Students must cope up with the new syllabus.
rightEx: Students must cope with the new syllabus.

rule: Comprise takes no of. If you want of, use consists of.
wrongEx: The team comprises of five officers.
rightEx: The team comprises five officers.

rule: Return already means go or give back. Back says it twice.
wrongEx: Return back the book on Monday.
rightEx: Return the book on Monday.

rule: Repeat means do again. Again is not needed.
wrongEx: Can you repeat again your name?
rightEx: Can you repeat your name?

rule: Severally means separately or one by one. For many times, say several times.
wrongEx: I have called him severally.
rightEx: I have called him several times.

rule: As a verb, request takes no for. As a noun, a request for is correct.
wrongEx: I request for your support.
rightEx: I request your support.

rule: The verb emphasise takes no on. The noun does: put emphasis on.
wrongEx: The teacher emphasised on discipline.
rightEx: The teacher emphasised discipline.

rule: Mention takes a direct object. Leave out about.
wrongEx: She mentioned about the meeting.
rightEx: She mentioned the meeting.

rule: Lose (one o) means to fail to keep. Loose (two o) means not tight.
wrongEx: I want to loose weight before December.
rightEx: I want to lose weight before December.

rule: Your shows ownership. You're is short for you are.
wrongEx: Thank you! Your welcome.
rightEx: Thank you! You're welcome.

rule: It's means it is. Its shows ownership, like his or her.
wrongEx: Its going to be a long day.
rightEx: It's going to be a long day.

rule: Advise (with s) is the verb. Advice (with c) is the noun.
wrongEx: I advice you to save money.
rightEx: I advise you to save money. That is good advice.

rule: Advice cannot be counted, so it has no plural. Say some advice or pieces of advice.
wrongEx: He gave me many advices.
rightEx: He gave me a lot of advice.

rule: Information has no plural. Say pieces of information.
wrongEx: We received informations from the chief.
rightEx: We received information from the chief.

rule: Furniture and equipment cannot be counted. They take no s.
wrongEx: The school bought new furnitures and equipments.
rightEx: The school bought new furniture and equipment.

rule: Affect is usually the verb: it affects you. Effect is usually the noun: the effect.
wrongEx: The rain will effect the harvest.
rightEx: The rain will affect the harvest. Its effect will be felt.

rule: Than compares. Then tells time or order.
wrongEx: Machakos is cooler then Kitui.
rightEx: Machakos is cooler than Kitui.

rule: Stationery (with e) is pens and paper. Stationary (with a) means not moving.
wrongEx: Buy envelopes from the stationary shop.
rightEx: Buy envelopes from the stationery shop. The bus is stationary.

rule: A principal is a head or main. A principle is a rule or belief.
wrongEx: The principle addressed the parents.
rightEx: The principal addressed the parents. Honesty is a principle.

rule: A compliment is praise. To complement is to complete or go well with.
wrongEx: He complemented her on the speech.
rightEx: He complimented her on the speech.

rule: As the subject, use I and he. A simple test: you would never say me went.
wrongEx: Me and him went to Machakos.
rightEx: He and I went to Machakos.

rule: Use fewer for things you can count, and less for things you cannot.
wrongEx: Less people attended this year.
rightEx: Fewer people attended this year. There was less noise.

rule: Equally and the same say one idea twice. Pick one.
wrongEx: Both answers are equally the same.
rightEx: Both answers are the same.

rule: Use for with a length of time and since with a starting point.
wrongEx: I have lived here since three years.
rightEx: I have lived here for three years, since 2023.

rule: Ensure means make sure. Insure means buy insurance cover.
wrongEx: Please insure the gate is locked.
rightEx: Please ensure the gate is locked.

rule: Breathe (with e) is the verb. Breath is the noun.
wrongEx: Take a deep breathe.
rightEx: Take a deep breath and breathe slowly.

rule: Bored is how you feel. Boring is what causes the feeling.
wrongEx: The meeting was long and I was boring.
rightEx: The meeting was boring, so I was bored.

wrong: I will pick you at the stage
right: I will pick you up at the stage
rule: To collect someone is to pick them up. To pick someone is to choose them.
wrongEx: I will pick you at six.
rightEx: I will pick you up at six.

rule: As a verb, order takes no for.
wrongEx: We ordered for two plates of pilau.
rightEx: We ordered two plates of pilau.

rule: Off is not a verb. Switch off, turn off or put off the lights.
wrongEx: Please off the lights before you sleep.
rightEx: Please switch off the lights before you sleep.

rule: A lot is always two words.
wrongEx: Thank you alot.
rightEx: Thank you a lot.

rule: Their shows ownership. There shows place. They're means they are.
wrongEx: There car is parked over their.
rightEx: Their car is parked over there.

rule: Whose shows ownership. Who's means who is.
wrongEx: Who's phone is ringing?
rightEx: Whose phone is ringing? Who's calling?

rule: On my way already means coming. One of them is enough.
wrongEx: Wait for me, I'm on my way coming.
rightEx: Wait for me, I'm on my way.

rule: To call off an event, cancel it. Cancel out means to balance something.
wrongEx: They cancelled out the meeting.
rightEx: They cancelled the meeting.

rule: Latter means the second of two. Later means after some time.
wrongEx: Between tea and coffee, I prefer the later.
rightEx: Between tea and coffee, I prefer the latter.

right: I wake up early every day
rule: Every day (two words) means each day. Everyday (one word) means ordinary.
wrongEx: I read the news everyday.
rightEx: I read the news every day. Slippers are everyday wear.
